newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed. [CORRECTED 09:48 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed. [CORRECTED 09:48 GMT]

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Thursday with investors uncertain about the near-term market trend and preferring to selling for quick profits, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 3,372 yuan ($407) per tonne, losing 18 yuan. It opened at 3,380 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,385 and a low of 3,370.
July rose 99 to 3,299, November fell two to 3,376 and the January 1998 contract 20 to 3,365 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 15,900 tonnes from 9,200 tonnes.
Soybean opened higher but profit-taking pushed prices steadily down for most of the session, traders said. Retail investors dominated the market, they said.

"Many investors took quick profits, being uncertain about the near-term trend," one trader said. "They were eager to liquidate their long positions at high levels, and this led to strong resistance at the 3,400-yuan level."
Traders said they expected retail investors to continue to dominate the market in next few days with institutions staying on the sidelines on a lack of market-moving news.
